[source] HALO-QA-20261029 EVAPORATION

**Hint**
Water molecules at the surface constantly gain energy from heat and their surroundings. When a molecule’s kinetic energy is high enough, it can break free into the air as vapour, even if the bulk liquid has not reached the boiling point.

**Why**
The source explains that evaporation “can occur below the boiling point because some surface molecules have enough energy to escape.” Heat adds energy to these molecules, raising the chance that some will overcome the liquid’s surface tension and leave.

**Next step**

[source] HALO-QA-20261029 EVAPORATION

**Hint**
Both processes turn liquid into vapour, but they differ in location. Evaporation only involves surface molecules, while boiling creates bubbles from the bulk liquid.

**Why**
The source states evaporation “can occur below the boiling point because some surface molecules have enough energy to escape.” Boiling “forms bubbles throughout a liquid at its boiling point.” Thus, evaporation happens at the surface, boiling occurs throughout.

**Next step**
Imagine a pot on a stove. At what temperature do bubbles first appear throughout the water? Your answer may cite [source].
